title: Code enforcement in Sebastian: the most common violations, how the process works, and who to call
seoTitle: Sebastian Code Enforcement: Common Violations, Process
description: Tall grass, swale parking, RVs and trailers: the code violations Sebastian sees most, how a case moves under Florida law, and how to report one.
dek: Most Sebastian code cases start with something small: tall grass, a car in the swale, a trailer in the driveway. Here is what the city looks for, how a case works, and how to stay on the right side of it.
facebook: Tall grass, a car parked in the swale, a trailer in the driveway — these are the code violations Sebastian sees most. Here's what the city watches for, how a case actually works, and who to call.

body.text: Nobody wants to find a code enforcement notice taped to the front door. In Sebastian, most cases are not about anything dramatic. They are about grass that got away from you during a rainy month, a car parked in the wrong spot, or a trailer that sat a little too long.
Here is what the City of Sebastian says it looks for, how a case works under Florida law, and what to do if you get a notice or need to report a problem next door.

body.title: The short version
body.text: Sebastian Code Enforcement is part of the Sebastian Police Department. The violations it lists most are trash and debris, overgrown grass and weeds, sign rules, noise, parking in swales, and oversized trailers and RVs. To report one, call 772-388-4436, option 1, or use the city's online form. Florida law does not allow anonymous complaints.
Who runs code enforcement in Sebastian

In Sebastian, Code Enforcement is a division of the Police Department, at 1201 Main Street. The city says the division answers complaints from residents and also opens cases on its own when officers see a problem.

The city's stated goal is to keep up "the beauty and character of the city." The rules themselves are in two places: the City Code of Ordinances and the Land Development Code. Both are posted online through Municode.
The city's Code Enforcement page names these as the most common issues:

items: Scattered trash, debris and litter on a property.
Overgrown grass and weeds.
Vacant lots that are overgrown onto a neighbor's improved property.
Sign code problems.
Noise.
Parking in swales.
Oversized trailers and recreational vehicles.

body.text: Swale parking is worth a closer look. Sebastian drains through its swales, the shallow grassy ditches along the street. Tires sink in, crush the ground and block the water. Parking there is one of the violations the city calls out by name.

Boats, trailers, campers and RVs are covered by Section 54-2-7.13 of the Land Development Code, titled "Mobile homes, travel trailers, campers, boats, trailers, and recreational vehicles." If you own one and keep it at home, read that section or call Code Enforcement before you assume your driveway is fine.
How a code case works in Florida
City code cases follow a state law, Chapter 162 of the Florida Statutes. Here is how it works in plain English.

items: An officer finds a violation, either from a complaint or on their own.
The officer gives the owner notice and a reasonable time to fix it. Notice can come by certified mail, by hand, or left at the home.
If it is fixed in time, that is usually the end of it.

If not, the case can go to a hearing before a code enforcement board or a special magistrate. A repeat violation, or one that is a serious threat to health or safety, can go to a hearing without a new correction period.
At the hearing, the board or magistrate can order the problem fixed and set a fine for each day it is not.

body.text: State law caps those daily fines. For most local governments, the limit is up to $250 a day for a first violation and up to $500 a day for a repeat violation. A violation that cannot be undone can bring up to $5,000. Places with 50,000 or more residents may set higher limits by ordinance. The board can also reduce a fine.
An unpaid fine order can be recorded as a lien on the property. State law says a lien like this cannot be foreclosed on a homestead. An owner can appeal a final order to circuit court within 30 days.

Sebastian uses a special magistrate for these hearings. In March 2025, the City Council approved a new one-year contract with a new special magistrate and asked staff to review the code enforcement process.

items: Read it closely. Note the violation, the code section and the date you have to fix it by.
Fix it as soon as you can, and take dated photos when it is done.
If you need more time, call Code Enforcement before the deadline and explain why.
If you think the notice is wrong, ask which code section applies and read it yourself on Municode.
If a hearing is set, go. You can speak and bring photos.

body.text: If you need to report a problem:

items: Call the Code Enforcement hotline at 772-388-4436, option 1. It takes messages 24 hours a day, and staff follow up the next business day.
Or use the online complaint form on the City of Sebastian's Code Enforcement page.
Give your name and address. Florida law says code officers cannot open a case from an anonymous complaint, except for an imminent threat to public health, safety or welfare.
For an emergency, call 911. For a non-emergency police matter, call 772-589-5233.

body.text: The easiest code case is the one that never starts. Keep the grass cut, keep cars out of the swale, and check the rules before the boat comes home.

faq.q: How do I report a code violation in Sebastian FL?
faq.a: Call the Sebastian Code Enforcement hotline at 772-388-4436, option 1, or use the online complaint form on the city's Code Enforcement page. You must give your name and address.

faq.q: Can I report a code violation anonymously in Sebastian?
faq.a: No. Florida law says a code officer cannot start a case from an anonymous complaint, unless there is an imminent threat to public health, safety, welfare or sensitive habitat.

faq.q: Can I park in the swale in Sebastian?
faq.a: Parking in swales is one of the violations Sebastian Code Enforcement lists as most common. Swales carry stormwater, and parking crushes and blocks them.

faq.q: Can I park my boat or RV in my driveway in Sebastian?
faq.a: The rules are in Section 54-2-7.13 of Sebastian's Land Development Code, which covers boats, trailers, campers and RVs. Oversized trailers and RVs are on the city's list of common violations, so check that section or call Code Enforcement first.

faq.q: How much can a code enforcement fine be in Florida?
faq.a: Under Chapter 162 of the Florida Statutes, most local governments can fine up to $250 a day for a first violation and up to $500 a day for a repeat violation, and up to $5,000 for a violation that cannot be undone.
